money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the South Sudanese Pound (SSP). South Sudan is a cash-based society. You'll need to pay cash in local currency or US dollars dated 2017 onwards for all purchases, including hotel bills. Shops and restaurants may refuse US dollar notes that are worn, damaged or marked. Exchange rates for SSP can vary significantly. It is recommended you carry sufficient funds in US dollars to cover expenses for the duration of your stay. Credit and debit cards, traveller's cheques and cash cards are generally not accepted. ATMs are scarce and often unreliable.

consular.notes: Australia doesn't have an embassy or consulate in South Sudan. For consular assistance, contact the Australian Embassy in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The security situation and other factors mean the Australian Government's ability to provide consular services in South Sudan is extremely limited.

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe and may include the death penalty.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Legal proceedings can be lengthy and ineffective. Be aware of your rights and responsibilities. Seek professional advice if you do anything that involves local legal matters. This is especially the case for family law matters, including: divorce child custody child support child abduction Penalties for criminal offences can include: death corporal punishment long jail term It is illegal to take any photos without a permit from the Ministry of Information. This includes photos taken with a mobile phone. don’t take pictures of government buildings, airports, vehicles, or persons in uniform keep your camera concealed and do not take random photos in public
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: Same-sex relationships are illegal in South Sudan and may lead to severe punishment, including lengthy jail terms. Discrimination based on sexual orientation is widespread and may lead to harassment by the public and police. LGBTQIA+ travellers should carefully consider the risks of travelling to South Sudan.

visa-preparation.entry_summary: Smartraveller advises Do not travel. A visa must be issued in advance through the Department of e-Visa and Immigration Services; entry is refused without one. The passport needs at least 5 blank pages. A yellow fever certificate is required.
visa-preparation.fastest_entry: e-Visa online: apply, pay by card, download the PDF within 72 hours.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Apply on evisa.gov.ss, pay by credit or debit card, download the e-visa PDF, and check the passport has 5 blank pages. Juba airport closes after dark.

steps.step: Create an account and complete the e-visa application.
Pay the fee online by credit or debit card and download the e-visa PDF (within 72 hours).
Carry a yellow fever certificate and expect screening at Juba airport.
To extend, contact the Ministry of the Interior in person.

documents: Passport with at least 5 blank pages
open_questions: What is the e-visa fee? The portal's front page doesn't show it.
